packageRules.description: Major Updates
Minor Updates
Patch Updates

Automerge patch, minor and digest updates. Every dependency that ships or builds this project is exercised by a CI job — two suites at a 99% floor, two strict mypy invocations, a 25-channel install matrix and hassfest — and Renovate only automerges on green, so a breaking bump fails the PR before it can merge. Runtime deps are declared as floors and no rangeStrategy is set, so a satisfied `>=` bound never moves: what lands here is the dev toolchain and the pinned action SHAs. Major updates, and the holds below, are reviewed by hand.

The shellcheck image pin is owned by the shared standard: it lives in the VENDORED packaging/shellcheck-all.sh, and this repo also carries an inline copy in the fork-PR workflow, which must stay byte-equal to it (a test asserts that). Renovate cannot move both halves consistently - bumping the vendored file fails the drift check, bumping only the workflow breaks the equality - so the bump happens in project-standard and arrives here as a re-vendor that updates both copies in one commit.

The shared standard lives on the self-hosted Forgejo, so the gitea-tags datasource has to be told which host to ask; there is no public registry to infer it from. Held for review rather than automerged: the post-upgrade task re-vendors the files on the branch, so the PR is complete, but a standard bump can change release machinery and that is worth a human read before it lands.
prBodyNotes: `refresh-pins.sh` re-vendors the standard at this tag on this branch, so the files and the lock should already agree with the pin. If the drift check still fails, the re-vendor did not run - check the task's output rather than re-vendoring by hand, because a manual fix here hides a broken automation.

packageRules.description: RELEASE-ONLY build pins: nothing in PR CI builds with them. publish.yml runs on a tag, and the install matrix tests artifacts that are already published — so a minor bump to the packager, the freezer, the manylinux image or the bundled interpreter merges on a green PR that never executed the changed build path, and fails at the next release instead. By then the PyPI upload has already happened, because that job does not wait for the packaging legs. Reviewed by hand, and proven by cutting a release candidate.
prBodyNotes: **CI cannot reach this.** Nothing in a pull request builds with this pin: `publish.yml` runs only on a tag, and the install matrix exercises artifacts that are already published. A green PR here says the code still lints and tests — it says nothing about whether the release still builds.
Clear it by cutting a release candidate with the bump in place, then merge.

packageRules.description: Grouped because the two arches are one upstream release and move to the same dated tag together: reviewing them apart shows the reviewer half the change, and a toolchain skew BETWEEN the arches is itself the risk the hand-review above exists to catch. Splitting them also doubles the rebase churn, since merging either one rebases the other open PR and restarts its checks. The regex versioning confines candidates to upstream's dated tags, so `latest` is never offered as an update. A branch opens only when BOTH arches have an update: Renovate's default group size of one would otherwise let whichever arch Quay published first arrive on its own, which is the single-arch review and the toolchain skew this grouping exists to prevent. The cost is that an update to one arch alone waits for the other, which is a publishing lag of hours because upstream cuts both from one release, not a state that persists.

bleak is the BLE transport provisioning speaks to the robot over. CI proves only that the code around it behaves: tests/test_ble_transport.py fakes the bleak boundary outright, and no runner has a Bluetooth radio, so scanning, pairing, GATT writes and the esp-idf protocomm exchange are never executed against the real library. Green CI therefore says nothing about the path that re-points a robot onto a new broker, so a bump is read by a human. Same reason dreame-valetudo holds pyusb — see its .renovaterc.json.
prBodyNotes: CI cannot reach the BLE path: no runner has a radio and the transport is faked at the bleak boundary. Bench-provisioning a real robot is what exercises this.

packageRules.description: The integration's pinned lib requirement is bumped by the release workflow, not Renovate.

release-macos.yml's `python-version` is not a test runner: PyInstaller freezes that exact interpreter into the shipped .pkg, so it has to move with PYTHON_VERSION in packaging/release-pins.env and the checksum a human reviews alongside it. The annotation hands the line to the cpython tag dep; disabling the built-in manager here leaves that dep as its only owner rather than an automerging second one that could ship a different Python than the Linux bundles carry.

This dep reads CPython's git tag, which has two consequences. The tag carries a leading `v` that no consumer accepts — setup-python resolves `python-version: v3.14.8` to nothing and the source build fetches `Python-v3.14.8.tar.xz`, which does not exist — so it is stripped here. And a tag exists before actions/python-versions publishes the manifest setup-python installs from, so a bump raised inside that window installs nothing; hold it until the manifest is certain to list it. Both are why the sibling project carries this identical rule.

setup-python resolves a version through actions/python-versions' versions-manifest.json, which that repo merges over an hour AFTER publishing the GitHub release Renovate reads. A bump raised inside that gap installs nothing: every python job on both forges dies at setup with 'version not found', which reads as a broken PR rather than an upstream artifact that has not landed yet. Hold each bump until the manifest is certain to list it.

These legs are compatibility FLOORS, not current-release aliases: the whole point is that a package which installs on the current release can still fail on the oldest one this project claims. Unclamped, Renovate bumps the tag and each floor quietly becomes a second current test — green, and proving nothing it was written to prove. Digests still refresh, so the images stay patched.

openSUSE's tag namespace still carries the legacy 42.x line, which sorts ABOVE 16.0 — so without this Renovate reads 42.3 as an upgrade from Leap 16 and proposes replacing the current qualification image with a release from the previous naming era. Verified against Docker Hub: `42` and `42.3` are both live tags. Digests still refresh.
Debian 13 is the deliberately selected current qualification host; Renovate refreshes its digest but a new Debian release is reviewed before replacing it.
Ubuntu 26.04 is the deliberately selected current qualification host; Renovate refreshes its digest but a new LTS is reviewed before replacing it.
Fedora 44 is the deliberately selected current qualification host; Renovate refreshes its digest but a future Fedora is reviewed after GA before replacing it.

DELIBERATELY OLD (see the block of rules sharing this prefix): this version is pinned low on purpose because something is tested against it. Renovate cannot know that newer is WORSE here — a bump deletes the test rather than updating it, and nothing goes red. The HA integration CI job must run whatever Python Home Assistant itself runs (3.13) — testing it on a newer one stops testing what users actually run, and installing HA there fails outright. No datasource maps a package to its supported Python, so Renovate cannot derive this; matched on the value because both jobs live in ci.yml. Raise this when HA moves.

DELIBERATELY OLD (see the block of rules sharing this prefix): this version is pinned low on purpose because something is tested against it. Renovate cannot know that newer is WORSE here — a bump deletes the test rather than updating it, and nothing goes red. 3.11.0 is the literal floor pyproject advertises (requires-python), and these jobs exist to prove the library still runs there. Renovate must not move even the patch: "3.11" resolves to the newest 3.11.x, which is a floor nobody actually has, and bumping deletes the test rather than updating it. Raise only together with requires-python.

DELIBERATELY OLD (see the block of rules sharing this prefix): this version is pinned low on purpose because something is tested against it. Renovate cannot know that newer is WORSE here — a bump deletes the test rather than updating it, and nothing goes red. macos-15 is the macOS support floor in ci-macos.yml, paired with macos-26 as current. A runner-image bump must never move the floor: that deletes the oldest-macOS coverage instead of updating it, and nothing goes red. Renovate's github-runners datasource is documented inconsistently on whether it extracts `macos-15` whole or splits it into depName `macos` / version `15`, and no bump has ever been observed here to settle it, so BOTH shapes are clamped. Whichever one is wrong is inert; a missing rule loses the floor.

DELIBERATELY OLD (see the block of rules sharing this prefix): this version is pinned low on purpose because something is tested against it. Renovate cannot know that newer is WORSE here — a bump deletes the test rather than updating it, and nothing goes red. Rocky 9 (glibc 2.34) is the .rpm smoke-test container in packaging/package-smoke-rpm.Dockerfile. It sits BELOW the build image (2.39) on purpose: PyInstaller links against the build machine's glibc, so a bundle can silently require 2.39, install cleanly anywhere and then refuse to start. Testing on Rocky 10 (also 2.39) means the binary always runs and the smoke test can never fail. Digests must keep flowing so the container stays patched, hence a range rather than disabling it.

customManagers.description: Docker images pinned tag@digest inside a workflow `docker` shell block, or in the packaging Dockerfiles. The github-actions manager does not look inside `run:` scripts and the dockerfile manager is not enabled, so without this every base image freezes at whatever digest it was pinned to.

Version pins annotated with a `# renovate:` comment — a shell assignment in packaging/release-pins.env, a `python-version:` key or a `pip install pkg==` line in the macOS release workflow. The tail is deliberately loose: the ANNOTATION is the anchor, and a pattern that only understood UPPERCASE="value" silently skipped the macOS half of the same two dependencies, so Renovate could bump Linux and leave macOS a version behind — the PyInstaller version and the CPython the Linux bundle is built from. Neither is a dependency of any manifest, so nothing else would ever bump them. They live in packaging/release-pins.env because two forges build this release (amd64 on Forgejo, arm64 on GitHub) and one file is what keeps them equal; a pattern listing only the workflows would silently stop bumping all of them.
